messages:
lia: Heads-up — CI started failing to apply sealed secrets into eu-west-2 after the new dedicated fleet onboarding. getting public key mismatch errors.

sam: saw that too. gitops-bot shows the secret-sync PR stuck, merge blocked.

deploy-bot: pipeline #4821 failed on job `sync-secrets`: exit code 1. logs attached.

alex: can you paste the exact error from the controller / kubeseal?

lia: error snippet: 
```
sealedsecrets-controller: failed to unseal data: public key mismatch: sealed secret was created with a different controller key (fingerprint: 3b:7a:...)
```
also seeing `kubeseal` client complaining when I try to re-seal in CI.

sam: this matches a key rotation we did via terraform for the sealed-secrets KMS wrapping key when spinning up the eu-west-2 cluster. I think the repo still has sealed secrets sealed with the old controller cert.

alex: timeline: we rotated the KMS key in module `infra.k8s.sealed_keys` on 2025-12-01, then applied. The controller in eu-west-2 now has new private key. Any sealedsecret objects sealed with the org-level cert (old) will be rejected.

lia: CI runners don't have the new cert file either — our encrypt/decrypt pipeline step expects to run `kubeseal --cert ./sealed-secrets.pem` but that file isn't in the runner image. We used to store the cert in the repo (bad), then moved to GCP KMS-sops. The new cluster KMS key is region-scoped so the runner in us-west can't decrypt the cert in eu-west.

sam: options: 1) re-seal all repo secrets with the eu-west controller cert (requires CI to get cert) 2) change GitOps to use external secrets (Vault/ExternalSecret operator) so we avoid sealed secrets entirely 3) ephemeral inject during deploy: pipeline fetches secret from Vault and kubectl creates secret at deploy time (no sealed secret stored).

alex: for immediate mitigation we should do (3) for the eu-west cluster to unblock the rollout. Medium-term we should standardize on Vault + ExternalSecrets/SealedSecrets policy. Also we need to reconcile terraform state referencing the wrong KMS key for other regions.

sam: small how-to for (1) re-seal with new cert if we go that route:
```
kubeseal --controller-name=sealed-secrets \
  --controller-namespace=kube-system \
  --cert ./eu-west2-sealed-secrets-pub.pem \
  < plain-secret.yaml > sealedsecret.yaml
```
But we need to get `eu-west2-sealed-secrets-pub.pem` into CI (encrypted via sops or pulled from Vault).

lia: trying (3) now as a quick patch: adding a pipeline step that runs vault login -> vault kv get -field=data secret/path/service-account | base64 -d -> kubectl create secret generic -n prod my-secret --from-literal=key=$(cat -) --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

deploy-bot: created pipeline run #4823 (ephemeral-inject). currently running.

sam: note: the pipeline runner role for eu-west doesn't have permission to read production vault path yet — updating IAM bind. PR: https://github.com/redwood/platform-infra/pull/567

alex: devops safety checklist before merging patch: 1) ensure audit logging on vault reads is enabled 2) rotate any plain secret exposure TTL in pipeline logs 3) use temp in-memory files, `--from-env-file` or `kubectl apply -f -` to avoid writing to disk.

lia: results: pipeline #4823 completed, secret created in cluster, Helm upgrade now progresses. This unblocks the model-serving rollout in eu-west.

sam: long term action items (assign):
- lia: write runbook for sealed-secrets key rotation (include kubeseal cert distribution patterns)
- sam: open RFC for moving secrets to ExternalSecrets backed by Vault (goal: avoid sealed-secrets cert distribution)
- alex: audit terraform modules that manage KMS keys and add region-tag checks to prevent unintended rotations.

lia: opened runbook draft: https://github.com/redwood/runbooks/pull/89
sam: RFC created: https://github.com/redwood/rfcs/pull/214
alex: terraform cleanup PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-modules/pull/332

lia: final note — if you rebuild a cluster in a new region, always export the controller public cert and add a `sealed-secrets-cert` artifact to the gitops repo (encrypted with sops) or push it to Vault. Do not rely on cross-region KMS decryptability without explicit IAM grants. :warning:

sam: agreed. tagging infra-owners for visibility. :eyes:
